content: Tokio uses a work-stealing scheduler. Tasks are spawned onto a thread pool where each worker thread maintains a local queue. When a worker's queue is empty, it steals tasks from other workers' queues. This approach balances load automatically without centralized coordination. The default thread pool size matches the number of CPU cores.

The Tokio runtime employs work-stealing for task scheduling. It maintains a pool of worker threads, each with its own local task queue. Idle workers take tasks from busy workers' queues to keep all cores utilized. This decentralized approach avoids bottlenecks from a single dispatch point. By default, the number of worker threads equals the available CPU core count.
